title: Bleecker and 11th
content: Yesterday in the West Village of New York City, a slice of afternoon light spotlit the brick apartments on the corner of Bleecker and 11th Avenue.What attracted me was the way the left tree was a dark pattern against the light building, while the central tree was a light texture against the cast shadow. Since my main interest was this tonal relationship, and since I only had a half hour to work, I limited my approach to a black and white wash drawing.I'm sitting on a park bench holding thewatercolor notebookon my knee. On the right is what the sketch looks like after about 10 minutes. At this stage I'm dropping in big tones over a rough perspective grid, careful to paint around the white of the branches and the windows.For the big tonal areas, I use twoNiji water brushes, one filled with water, and the other filled withHiggins Eternal ink. The light gray areas are the clear water brush picking up a little ink.Here's a detail of a section the size of a postage stamp. After the big washes dry, I use a blackwatercolor pencilfor the linear details of the windows, mullions, cornice details, and small branches.
